chains.title: HOXB13 binding at the T allele contributes to RFX6 regulation
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, which the literature describes as an rs339331-associated prostate cancer risk enhancer.
chains.cell_type: Prostate cancer cells in which the reported rs339331 enhancer and HOXB13 binding are active; activity in LNCaP clone FGC is not established.

links.claim: HOXB13 is the candidate because the literature reports increased HOXB13 binding at the rs339331 region in T-risk versus C-protective homozygous cell lines. This supports greater binding for T (ref), but does not isolate HOXB13 from other enhancer-complex members in every context. No QBiC-SELEX result is provided.
The variant lies within enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, and the literature places a HOXB13-containing transcriptional complex at the rs339331-associated enhancer.
RFX6 is the proposed target: the literature reports increased RFX6 transcription associated with T and increased HOXB13 binding at the region, and RFX6 has strong locus-to-gene support.
The proposed binding and regulatory effect is in prostate cancer cells represented by the cited functional studies; the supplied evidence does not establish HOXB13 occupancy in LNCaP clone FGC.

The reported T-associated HOXB13 binding and RFX6 transcription could connect the enhancer to prostate cancer, but a causal contribution to risk is not established. The reported T-risk direction conflicts with the C effect allele listed for prostate cancer in the GWAS Catalog.

predictions: In relevant prostate cancer cells, allele-specific assays will show greater HOXB13 occupancy on T than C, and HOXB13 perturbation will reduce the corresponding allele-dependent RFX6 effect.
HOXB13 occupancy and perturbation will explain the allele-dependent effect better than AR occupancy and perturbation do.
falsified_if: Allele-specific assays in a relevant prostate cancer context show no greater HOXB13 binding on T than C.
HOXB13 perturbation leaves the allele-dependent enhancer activity and RFX6 expression unchanged, while AR perturbation removes the effect.

chains.title: AR occupancy at the T allele contributes to RFX6 regulation
chains.element: The variant lies in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909; literature describes the site as an AR-binding site in prostate cancer tumors.
chains.cell_type: Prostate cancer tumor cells with the reported reprogrammed AR-binding state; this state is not established in LNCaP clone FGC.

links.claim: AR is a candidate because the literature reports greater AR chromatin occupancy for T (ref) than C (alt) at rs339331 in prostate cancer tumors. No QBiC-SELEX result is provided. ENCODE reports no TF peaks in LNCaP clone FGC, so occupancy in that cell line is unconfirmed.
The variant lies within enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909. The cCRE's reported SCREEN scores are maxima across biosamples and do not establish activity in the proposed tumor state.
RFX6 is the leading target candidate because it is nearby, has the strongest locus-to-gene support among the listed genes, and is linked in the literature to this prostate cancer locus.
This model requires prostate cancer tumor cells with the reported reprogrammed AR-bound state; the supplied ENCODE data do not show TF occupancy at the variant in LNCaP clone FGC.

Greater AR occupancy on T could contribute to prostate cancer risk through altered RFX6 regulation, but that causal chain is not directly established. The reported T risk direction conflicts with the C effect allele listed for prostate cancer in the GWAS Catalog.

predictions: In prostate tumor cells with the reported AR-bound state, allele-specific assays will show greater AR occupancy on T than C.
AR perturbation will reduce the T-associated regulatory effect more than HOXB13 perturbation does; this has not been demonstrated by the supplied evidence.
falsified_if: Allele-specific assays in a relevant prostate tumor context show no greater AR occupancy on T than C.
AR perturbation leaves the allele-dependent enhancer activity and RFX6 expression unchanged in the proposed context.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: The variant will not produce a reproducible allele-specific TF-occupancy change that alters enhancer activity or RFX6 expression in relevant prostate cells.
The association may reflect linkage to another causal variant or another mechanism not mediated by TF binding at this base.
falsified_if: Isogenic allele replacement or allele-specific assays reproducibly show that changing this base changes TF occupancy and enhancer activity or RFX6 expression in relevant prostate cells.

grades_v0.reason: The quoted literature reports greater AR occupancy for T at rs339331 in prostate cancer tumors, but no QBiC-SELEX result is provided. ENCODE reports no AR peak in LNCaP clone FGC, so occupancy in that cell line is unconfirmed.
E03 directly places the variant within enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, and E09c describes the rs339331 site as an AR-binding site in prostate cancer tumors.
RFX6 is nearby, has the strongest reported L2G support among the listed genes, and E09d identifies it as the susceptibility gene whose expression is increased at the risk-associated enhancer.
E09c places the reprogrammed AR-bound site in prostate cancer tumors. The chain appropriately distinguishes this context from LNCaP clone FGC, where E04 reports no matching-biosample TF peaks.

The evidence supports a prostate cancer association and reports greater AR occupancy for T, but does not directly connect that allele-specific occupancy to RFX6 expression or cancer risk. The direction also conflicts with E06, which lists C as the prostate cancer association effect allele.

E09d reports a GATA2/SMAD4 complex with HOXB13 at the risk-associated enhancer, which is relevant occupancy evidence. It does not establish allele-specific GATA2 binding, and no QBiC-SELEX result is provided; the proposed T-greater-than-C direction is provisional.
E03 directly places the variant in enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909, and E09d describes a transcriptional complex at the rs339331-associated enhancer.
E09d directly says the reported complex at the risk-associated enhancer leads to increased RFX6 expression; E07 also gives RFX6 the strongest locus-to-gene support.
E09d places the complex at a prostate cancer risk-associated enhancer. The evidence does not establish its activity in LNCaP clone FGC, which the chain acknowledges.

The enhancer-complex-to-RFX6 link is reported, but the proposed allele-specific GATA2 effect and its contribution to risk are conditional and unmeasured. The proposed T direction is also inconsistent with E06's C effect allele for prostate cancer.

grades_final.reason: The quoted literature reports greater AR occupancy on T at rs339331 in prostate cancer tumors, but no QBiC-SELEX result is provided; ENCODE shows no peak in LNCaP.
E03 directly places the variant within enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2496909; the claim appropriately does not infer activity in the proposed tumor state from biosample-maximized scores.
RFX6 has the strongest reported locus-to-gene support among the nearby candidates in E07, and the cited literature links RFX6 to rs339331.
E09c reports the T-associated AR occupancy in prostate cancer tumors, while E04 supports the stated caveat that occupancy is unconfirmed in LNCaP.

The locus is associated with prostate cancer and the literature reports T as the risk allele, but the proposed causal path through AR and RFX6 is not established; E06 lists C as the GWAS effect allele, creating a direction discrepancy.
E10d reports increased HOXB13 binding at the region in T-risk versus C-protective homozygous lines, but no QBiC-SELEX result is provided.
E03 directly places the variant in the enhancer-like cCRE, and E09d/E10d place the HOXB13-containing complex at the rs339331-associated enhancer.
E10d reports increased RFX6 transcription with the T allele and increased HOXB13 binding, while E07 provides locus-to-gene support for RFX6.

The cited evidence places the enhancer and binding in a prostate-cancer context, but the supplied quotes do not identify the relevant cell lines or establish HOXB13 occupancy in a specific prostate cell type; LNCaP occupancy is unconfirmed.

The cited allele-associated enhancer and RFX6 observations are consistent with a prostate-cancer contribution, but do not establish that HOXB13-mediated regulation causes risk; E06 lists C rather than T as the GWAS effect allele.

matrix.test: Allele-specific AR and HOXB13 CUT&RUN (or ChIP) at rs339331 in a relevant prostate cancer model heterozygous for T/C

outcomes.outcome: Greater AR occupancy on T than C; the AR allelic difference is the distinguishing result.
Greater HOXB13 occupancy on T than C; the HOXB13 allelic difference is the distinguishing result.
No reproducible allelic occupancy difference for either TF.

matrix.test: Perturb AR and HOXB13 separately in the same prostate cancer model, then measure allele-specific enhancer activity and RFX6 expression

outcomes.outcome: AR perturbation preferentially reduces the allele-dependent enhancer or RFX6 effect.
HOXB13 perturbation preferentially reduces the allele-dependent enhancer or RFX6 effect.
Neither perturbation reveals a reproducible variant-dependent regulatory effect.

matrix.test: Isogenic T-to-C and C-to-T editing followed by RFX6 expression and enhancer-activity measurement in a relevant prostate cancer model

outcomes.outcome: Editing changes enhancer activity or RFX6 expression in a direction consistent with the T-associated AR model.
Editing changes enhancer activity or RFX6 expression in a direction consistent with the T-associated HOXB13 model.
Editing produces no reproducible regulatory change attributable to this base.

next_experiment: The cheapest proposed test that separates the two leading chains is allele-specific AR and HOXB13 CUT&RUN at rs339331 in a relevant T/C-heterozygous prostate cancer model. It directly compares the competing TF-occupancy predictions; LNCaP clone FGC is not an established occupancy-positive context in the supplied data.

Dysregulated expression or mutations of the RFX6 gene in prostate cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, melanoma, and other tumors have garnered significant interest, with studies showing that such alterations affect tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, and are correlated with an unfavorable clinical prognosis in patients carrying RFX6 mutations.

Here the FinnGen cohort phenome-wide analysis, along with multiple genome-wide association studies, has consistently identified the rs339331-RFX6/6q22 locus associated with prostate cancer (PCa) risk across diverse populations.
It is uncovered that rs339331 resides in a reprogrammed androgen receptor (AR) binding site in PCa tumors, with the T risk allele enhancing AR chromatin occupancy.

Strinkingly, GATA2 and SMAD4 globally mediated inherited PCa risk and formed a transcriptional complex with HOXB13 at the PCa risk-associated rs339331/6q22 enhancer, leading to increased expression of the PCa susceptibility gene RFX6.
Notable genes of interest include HCP5, RFX6 and H3C1 for risk, and MKI67 and KLF5 for aggressive disease.
